issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising second appellate jurisdiction may not interfere with concurrent factual findings unless they are contrary to law, contrary to the pleadings or evidence, or wholly perverse.
material_facts: The trial court and the first appellate court both dismissed the suit after assessing the evidence and finding that the plaintiffs had not proved the requirements for a perpetual injunction.
The High Court allowed the second appeal and decreed the suit without identifying a legal defect or perversity in the concurrent findings.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in interfering with the concurrent factual findings; its decision was set aside and the dismissal of the suit was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Concurrent findings of fact based on appreciation of the facts and evidence bind a High Court in second appeal unless they are contrary to law, contrary to the pleadings or evidence, or wholly perverse. The judgment cites no specific statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

rule.if: second_appeal and concurrent_factual_findings and not (findings_contrary_to_law or findings_contrary_to_record or findings_wholly_perverse)

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding before the higher court is a second appeal.
predicates.concurrent_factual_findings: The trial court and the first appellate court reached the same factual findings after considering the evidence.
predicates.findings_contrary_to_law: The concurrent findings conflict with a governing rule of law.
predicates.findings_contrary_to_record: The concurrent findings conflict with the pleadings or evidence on the record.
predicates.findings_wholly_perverse: The concurrent findings are wholly perverse.
predicates.high_court_interference_not_permitted: The High Court does not interfere with the concurrent factual findings.

issues.definition: When a matter is before a High Court in second appeal and the lower courts have made concurrent factual findings, the High Court does not interfere unless those findings conflict with law or the record, or are wholly perverse.

issues.legal_issue: A co-sharer cannot obtain a perpetual injunction against another co-sharer, or a transferee from that co-sharer, merely by claiming possession of jointly owned property without proving exclusion and ouster.
material_facts: The suit property formed part of land inherited by several brothers.
The defendants had purchased the suit land from one co-sharer, while the plaintiffs were the sons of another co-sharer.
The plaintiffs sought a perpetual injunction and claimed possession, but the lower courts found that they had not proved exclusive possession to the exclusion of the other co-sharers.
The plaintiffs did not establish a denial of the other co-sharers’ rights to their knowledge followed by exclusion and ouster for the statutory period.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs were not entitled to an injunction against the purchasers, who had stepped into the shoes of their co-sharer vendor and could defend their title and possession.
issues.legal_principle: Possession by one co-sharer is possession by all and is not adverse to the others unless the person in possession denies their rights to their knowledge and exclusion and ouster follow for the statutory period. A purchaser from a co-sharer steps into the vendor’s shoes and may defend the vendor’s title and possession. The Court relied on Mohammad Baqar & Ors. v. Naim-un-Nisa Bibi & Ors. (AIR 1956 SC 548); it cited no specific statutory provision.

rule.if: injunction_suit and claimant_is_cosharer and defendant_is_transferee_from_cosharer and not ouster_proved

predicates.injunction_suit: The proceeding seeks an injunction concerning possession of property.
predicates.claimant_is_cosharer: The claimant holds an interest in the property as a co-sharer.
predicates.defendant_is_transferee_from_cosharer: The defendant acquired the relevant interest from another co-sharer.
predicates.ouster_proved: The claimant establishes a denial of the other co-sharers’ rights to their knowledge followed by exclusion and ouster for the statutory period.
predicates.injunction_unavailable: The claimant is not entitled to the injunction against the defendant.

issues.definition: A claimant who is a co-sharer cannot obtain an injunction against a transferee from another co-sharer where the claimant has not proved exclusion and ouster.
